title: The Tally at Copper Creek
text: A prospecting camp's daily gold tally rises after the sluice is shut down, though nobody brings ore into camp. Create a frontier mystery narrated by the cook, who knows each miner's appetite better than their alibi.

title: One Extra Stitch
text: A tailor repairing a ceremonial flag finds a hidden stitch pattern that matches no national or military code. Let the tailor and a young archivist decode it, while leaving open whether its maker wanted the message found.

title: The Child Who Knew the Tide Tables
text: A coastal schoolchild predicts an unusually high tide using calculations no one taught them, then refuses to say where they learned the method. Follow the teacher's inquiry toward a submerged structure and a secret that adults have mistaken for folklore.

title: The Pianist's Green Fingertips
text: A conservatory doctor finds green staining on the fingers of every musician who has practiced in one particular room. Write a short mystery about a substitute instructor tracing the pigment to a concealed repair made during wartime.

title: The Last Crate of Oranges
text: A produce broker's final crate arrives at a market with fruit from a region that has had no harvest in years. The market porter investigates the supplier, discovering that several merchants have been waiting for this exact shipment.

title: The Bead on the Magistrate's Desk
text: A single glass bead appears on the magistrate's desk after every hearing involving a land dispute. Write a courtroom-adjacent mystery from the perspective of a court interpreter who notices which litigants never see it.

title: A Census of Unclaimed Shoes
text: A repair shop owner keeps a shelf of shoes whose owners never return, but one pair is collected every year by a different person who knows its worn sole intimately. Build a mystery about a community's shared attempt to preserve one stranger's route.

title: The Window Tax Collector
text: In a city where buildings are taxed by their visible windows, an inspector discovers a block whose count changes depending on the hour. Write a speculative mystery about architecture, evasion, and the tenant who insists every window belongs to someone.

title: The Orchard of Paper Leaves
text: An artist decorates a dead tree with paper leaves, each bearing the name of a person who denies ever visiting the village. Let a mail carrier investigate the names and find that the tree may be recording departures rather than arrivals.

title: The Quartermaster's Quiet Inventory
text: A ship's quartermaster reports that no supplies are missing, yet the crew has been rationed for weeks. Write a claustrophobic sea mystery from the quartermaster's inventory sheets, where every entry is accurate and the total is impossible.

title: Moths in the Courtroom Vent
text: A courthouse ventilation system releases moths only during testimony about a decades-old fire. A court reporter begins tracking their emergence and finds a connection between the building's renovations and a witness who has never been called.

title: The Diver's Unlisted Catch
text: A deep-sea diver returns from a routine salvage mission with a small brass instrument that does not appear on the wreck's manifest. Give the diver's sibling, a marine conservator, the task of deciding whether to report the object or learn why the wreck was altered.

title: The Tailor Who Sewed for No One
text: A tailor's ledger records custom measurements for clients who never arrive, and each set fits a different person in the neighborhood. Write a mystery about why the tailor refuses to destroy the measurements, using the tailor's private monologue as the form.

title: A Map of Warm Pavement
text: A city engineer's winter temperature survey reveals a warm line beneath the streets that traces a route no utility plan records. Follow a night crew as they uncover what is heating the pavement and who has been following the same path for years.

title: The Dog Show's Empty Ribbon
text: A judge awards first prize at a dog show, then discovers the ribbon has been cut from every photograph of the winning animal. Write a light, observant mystery about reputation, ownership, and the one handler who refuses to enter again.

title: The Locksmith's Uncut Blank
text: A locksmith finds an uncut key blank inside a lock that has not been opened in thirty years. The blank carries a faint imprint of a hand that matches no living customer; make the investigation hinge on craft knowledge rather than a supernatural explanation.

title: The Seamstress's Blue Receipt
text: A seamstress receives payment in a currency withdrawn before she was born, but the bills are accepted by a shopkeeper across the street. Write a mystery that follows the money through the neighborhood and reveals why two people are willing to pretend it is valid.

title: The Choir's Unassigned Breath
text: A choir director hears one extra breath between phrases during rehearsal, although every singer can be accounted for. Create a rehearsal-room screenplay where the singers gradually realize the breath is being produced by someone trying to hide a different sound.

title: The Canal's Dry Lock
text: A canal lock empties overnight without losing water downstream, and a barge trapped inside is suddenly carrying twice its declared cargo. Let a lock keeper investigate the hydraulic puzzle and the crew's carefully divided loyalties.

title: The Archivist's Unfamiliar Hand
text: A handwriting analyst identifies an anonymous threat as the work of someone whose hands were injured before the message could have been written. Ask what kind of evidence could persuade the analyst—and whether certainty is worth the cost.

title: A Parcel of Unripe Plums
text: A village grocer receives the same parcel of unripe plums every spring, but this year one fruit contains a small ceramic token. Let the grocer trace the parcel's route through neighboring farms without knowing whether the sender wants a debt repaid or a crime remembered.

title: The Maskmaker's Missing Mold
text: During a masked festival, the mold for the town's oldest face disappears, and by dawn one reveler has vanished from the guest list. Write a mystery in which every disguise is locally recognizable, but none can be trusted as an identity.

title: The Lighthouse Lensmaker's Error
text: A retired lensmaker claims the beacon's beam has been sweeping a different arc for years, though ship logs show no change. A trainee keeper investigates what the beam was meant to signal to someone on shore.

title: Notes from the Lost Property Desk
text: At a convention center, an attendant notices that the objects people claim are never the objects they first reported missing. Compose the story as short lost-property forms and let their discrepancies expose an unseen exchange among attendees.

title: The Weaver's Narrow Cloth
text: A loom produces a strip of cloth exactly one handspan too short for every order, though its settings have not changed. Write a workshop mystery about the apprentice who measures the finished fabric and discovers a different pattern in each customer's complaint.

title: The Inspector's Unopened Lunch
text: A food-safety inspector's lunch remains untouched at every restaurant they visit, yet each kitchen begins preparing the same dish before the inspector arrives. Follow the inspector as they seek the person coordinating the kitchens and the warning hidden in the menu.

title: The Salt Line on the Nursery Wall
text: A conservation worker finds a salt line in a long-dry nursery, but it lies above the highest recorded flood level. Write a house-history mystery where the caretaker's childhood measurements matter more than the official surveys.

title: The Clerk Who Counted Applause
text: At a provincial theater, the applause after one actor's entrance is always shorter than the rest, even when the actor is replaced. Write a backstage mystery from the understudy's perspective, where the audience's response may be a signal rather than a judgment.

title: The Surveyor's Crooked Horizon
text: A bridge survey team agrees that the riverbank is level, but every instrument shows the horizon tilted by precisely the same degree. Build a mystery around an engineer who suspects the measurements are correct and the landscape has been rearranged.

title: A Recipe Written in Weights
text: A baker inherits a recipe measured only in the weights of kitchen tools, and each attempt produces a loaf that tastes like a different memory. Make the investigation about an old bakery's ownership dispute, where the recipe is evidence but not a confession.

title: The Brass Tag at the Menagerie
text: A zoo keeper discovers a brass tag attached to the enclosure of an animal that was never part of the collection. Let the keeper trace the tag's serial number through a defunct traveling menagerie and confront the curator who remembers it.

title: The Bellows in the Abandoned Forge
text: A blacksmith hears the old forge's bellows moving at night, although the mechanism has been dismantled and stored. Write a mystery about a new tenant who wants the noise stopped and the blacksmith who hopes it continues.

title: The Cart of Unripe Melons
text: A market porter finds a cart of unripe melons parked each dawn at a different stall, with no seller and no price. The merchants begin competing to claim it; give one porter a reason to discover who is using the fruit to settle a score.

title: The Glazier's Two Reflections
text: A glazier replacing a shopfront finds that passersby appear twice in the old glass, but only one reflection carries a parcel. Make the mystery resolve through an ordinary flaw in the glass—or let the glazier argue that the flaw is the least important part.

title: The Absent Captain's Knot
text: A fishing crew discovers a knot tied in a style their missing captain swore never to use. Write a tense story at sea in which each sailor can tie it, but only one knows what the knot was meant to secure.

title: The Museum Guard's Sunday Route
text: A museum guard's Sunday patrol consistently takes seven minutes longer than the same route on any other day, though the galleries are empty. Let a newly hired conservator follow the guard and discover a room that is not on the staff's official floor plan.

title: The Pigeon Fancier's Wrong Loft
text: A prized racing pigeon returns to the wrong loft carrying a thread from a ceremonial sash. Write a neighborhood mystery about the bird's route, the fancier's rivalry, and why the sash's owner insists the thread was never missing.

title: An Almanac of Unseasonal Fruit
text: A rural almanac predicts the exact dates when fruit will ripen on trees that have been cut down. Give a skeptical orchard apprentice three days to determine whether the predictions are fraud, inherited knowledge, or a warning about a coming land sale.

title: The Judge's Borrowed Gavel
text: A courtroom gavel goes missing between two hearings, and the replacement sounds different enough to change how witnesses answer. Write from the clerk's viewpoint as a seemingly trivial swap exposes a deliberate attempt to influence testimony.

title: The Brass Compass at Low Tide
text: A salvage crew finds a compass that points toward the shore only when the tide is falling. Let the youngest diver trace its owner through a sequence of coastal trades, discovering why the object was deliberately left behind.

title: The Night the Kiln Cooled Early
text: A pottery kiln cools twelve hours ahead of schedule, ruining a shipment but leaving one vessel untouched. Write a mystery about a cooperative workshop where every maker had access to the controls and only one had reason to save that piece.

title: The Translator's Missing Verb
text: A diplomatic interpreter receives a transcript in which every sentence is complete except for one verb that no language dictionary can supply. Use the interpreter's letters to a former mentor to uncover whether the omission is linguistic, political, or personal.

title: The Sawmill's Uncut Beam
text: A carpenter orders a beam from a closed sawmill and receives a piece of timber bearing fresh tool marks. Investigate the mill's final days through the lumber's grain, and let the carpenter decide whether identifying its maker will help or harm the living.

title: The Pale Horse in the Parade
text: A parade's white horse refuses to pass one particular house, though it has walked the route for years. Write a mystery from the perspective of the child carrying the banner, who discovers the house's connection to a vanished parade marshal.

title: The Watchmaker's Unwound Spring
text: A watchmaker finds every repaired clock in a neighborhood has stopped at a different time, but all were wound by the same person. Build a character-driven mystery about the repair route and a customer who has been paying in stories instead of money.

title: The Clinic's Unused Waiting Number
text: A clinic's ticket dispenser skips a number every day, and the skipped patients appear in no appointment system. Let a receptionist investigate the pattern while protecting a colleague who believes the missing numbers are keeping someone safe.

title: The Eel Seller's Silver Scale
text: A fish seller finds a silver scale among the day's eels, though the river has no fish of that kind. Write a river-town mystery about an old flood, a vanished boat, and the seller's reluctance to let anyone test the scale.

title: A Blueprint for the Wrong Stair
text: A building inspector finds a staircase in a new school that does not connect to any floor shown on the plans. Create a mystery where the architect, janitor, and student all offer plausible reasons for its existence, none of them quite compatible.

title: The Orchard's Night Pollinators
text: An ecologist studying a rare moth finds that its population peaks only on evenings when the village's streetlamps are switched off. Her field notes lead to an old agreement between residents, and to the one person who has begun breaking it.

title: The Taxidermist's Unfinished Hare
text: A taxidermist leaves one hare unfinished for decades, despite completing every other commission. When a former apprentice returns with a matching specimen, write the mystery of what the taxidermist recognized and why silence became part of the craft.

title: The Signalman's Red Mitten
text: A rail signalman's red mitten is found at a crossing miles from the line, and a train arrives there ten minutes later than its schedule says it should. Write a period mystery about how a delay was created without altering a single timetable.

title: The Orchard Gate's Three Hinges
text: A farm gate has three hinges though it is too small to need more than two, and a new hinge appears after every harvest. Let a seasonal worker uncover why the family keeps replacing one hinge and what the gate once enclosed.

title: The Tail End of the Parade
text: Every year, one extra banner is returned to the parade committee after the procession, though no participant remembers carrying it. Write a warm mystery in which a retiring banner-maker tries to identify the quiet volunteer who has kept the tradition alive.

title: The Librarian of Edible Ink
text: A rare manuscript's ink can be read only after a page is dampened with a particular tea, but each reading erases a word. Ask a conservator to choose which passage to reveal when the missing text may settle a centuries-old dispute.

title: The Carpenter's False Corner
text: A carpenter is hired to square a room that measures perfectly on every wall yet has no right angle. Write a domestic mystery about the previous owner's renovations and the one corner that has been left untouched through three remodels.

title: The Dyer's Unclaimed Red
text: A textile dyer produces a red no customer ordered, and people from across town begin arriving to ask for it by a name the dyer has never heard. Follow the dyer's search for the colour's origin, letting each claimant tell a different version of the same event.

title: The Estate's Crooked Orchard
text: An estate's fruit trees lean toward a wall that is straight according to every survey. A groundskeeper discovers that the trees were replanted in a precise pattern after a private burial, but no one agrees who was meant to be remembered.

title: The Violin Bow with Two Owners
text: Two musicians arrive at a repair shop with identical bows, each bearing wear patterns that match the other's playing style. Let the luthier investigate the instruments' journey without deciding too quickly which musician is lying.

title: The Street Sweeper's Pale Dust
text: A street sweeper finds a fine white dust along a route that has no construction nearby, and it vanishes before the morning inspection. Write a city mystery about the route, the missing source, and a sweeper whose careful records are dismissed as superstition.

title: The Orchard Bell's Sunday Silence
text: A bell used to scare birds from an orchard stops ringing on Sundays, though no one changes its mechanism. Let a new caretaker investigate who has been disabling it and why the birds' one quiet day matters to the harvest workers.

title: The Apprentice's Unfinished Portrait
text: A portrait restorer discovers that the unfinished face beneath a later painting belongs to someone who was never listed among the household's residents. Write a layered mystery about who commissioned the cover-up and why the restorer's own family name appears on the frame.

title: A Bridge of Borrowed Timber
text: After a flood, a temporary bridge contains planks stamped with the marks of five different sawmills, two of them long closed. Tell the mystery through the bridge inspector's field journal as the town argues over whether to preserve or dismantle it.

title: The Conservatory's Unseasonal Frost
text: One bench in a heated conservatory is rimed with frost each dawn, while every plant on it remains healthy. A night gardener investigates the airflow and discovers a visitor has been using the cold patch to protect something far more fragile than a flower.

title: The Clocktower's New Shadow
text: A clocktower casts a second shadow only during the town's annual blackout, and the shadow falls across a building demolished before the tower was built. Make a concise speculative mystery about what the shadow marks and who has been waiting for it.

title: The Fishmonger Who Never Bought Ice
text: A fishmonger's stall stays cold through a heatwave without using ice, refrigeration, or electricity. Write a mystery from the perspective of a rival vendor who starts investigating for business reasons and uncovers a much older arrangement with the harbor.

title: The Last Page of the Atlas
text: A school atlas contains a final page glued to the back cover, showing a country omitted from every edition and absent from every student's geography exam. Give a geography teacher and a skeptical pupil one afternoon to discover who keeps adding the page—and why.

title: The Night Custodian's Chalk Marks
text: A night custodian marks each room they clean with a small chalk symbol, but the marks form a route through the building that no one recognizes. Write a mystery about what the route reveals, and let the custodian choose whether the pattern should be erased before morning.

title: The Salt Accountant of Veyra
text: In a cliffside city where salt is the only legal measure of wealth, an apprentice accountant discovers that the treasury's ledgers balance only because one household is being charged for the sea. Write the story of what she risks when she corrects the books.

title: A Choir for the Unhatched
text: The royal hatchery employs singers to coax unborn phoenixes from their shells, but the new conductor hears one egg keeping time to a song no human knows. Build a screenplay scene around the rehearsal that follows.

title: Milepost Nine Has Moved
text: A courier crossing the northern moor finds that every milepost has shifted one mile closer to the capital, though her map and pace are sound. Tell what the road is trying to deliver through her.

title: The Orchard That Refuses Kings
text: An ancient orchard yields fruit to anyone who asks politely, except crowned rulers, whom its trees pelt with hard green pears. A newly elected monarch arrives incognito to learn whether the trees object to the crown or to the person beneath it.

title: A Taxonomy of Unmade Monsters
text: A field naturalist catalogs creatures that exist only in the margins of unfinished maps, and one specimen has begun following the expedition's corrections. Write an entry that gradually becomes a confession.

title: The Baker Who Feeds Comets
text: Once each winter, a baker climbs a bell tower to leave warm seed-cakes for the comets that pass close enough to smell them. This year a comet arrives early and asks, in crumbs, for a different kind of help.

title: The Cloud's Unmapped Reply
text: An apprentice weather-keeper must write apology letters to every village flooded after the king redirects an enchanted rain cloud. A reply arrives from a settlement absent from every royal map, asking her to return the cloud one drop at a time.

title: The Candlewright's Apprenticeship
text: A candlewright can make a flame burn blue for courage, green for patience, or gold for a truth someone is ready to hear. Her newest apprentice keeps producing a color neither of them can name; follow their experiments toward an unexpected consequence.

title: When the Staircase Reached the Clouds
text: A stair-builder's latest commission rises through the clouds and ends at a landing where the wind has been waiting with a grievance. Tell the tale from the point of view of the lowest step.

title: The Queen's Unlicensed Alchemist
text: In a kingdom where every transformation requires a permit, a village alchemist turns a field of stones into bread after the grain blight. Write a monologue for the clerk ordered to prosecute her, who has just eaten a loaf.

title: Instructions for Growing a Giant
text: A farming cooperative receives a packet of seeds labeled only with a height and a warning about harvest etiquette. Compose the village's practical growing guide, including the disagreement over what counts as ripe.

title: The Last Bellmaker of Orra
text: Every bell in Orra rings to announce a future event, but the old bellmaker's final commission remains stubbornly silent. Write the story of the child who volunteers to test it on the night before the town elects its next mayor.

title: A Parliament of Painted Horses
text: The painted horses on the council chamber's murals convene after midnight to debate a law that will erase their mountain homeland from official maps. Stage their argument as a screenplay scene in which no one can leave the painted wall.

title: The Riverboat's Unpaid Passenger
text: A boatman accepts no fare from the tiny bronze passenger who boards at every lock, yet each stop leaves him with a new debt owed to someone downstream. Develop a story in which he discovers what the passenger is collecting.

title: The Library of Rainfall Permits
text: In a drought-stricken plateau, clerks issue permits for each cloudburst, down to the last cupful. One applicant requests rain for a patch of ground that appears on no survey; write the clerk's account of the hearing.

title: A Small Manual for Exorcising Manners
text: A etiquette tutor is called to a manor where every guest's worst habit has taken physical form: interrupting is a flock of starlings, vanity a gilded mask. Create a playful set of lessons that turns into a rescue plan.

title: The Copper Orchard's Night Shift
text: Workers in an orchard of metal trees must harvest the copper fruit before it rings itself loose and rolls into the ravine. One new picker finds a warm seed inside a fruit and hides it in her lunch pail.

title: The Saint of Unfinished Roads
text: A roadside shrine is dedicated to a saint who blesses journeys that never reach their destination. A pilgrim arrives demanding the blessing be withdrawn before her son sets out; let the shrine's keeper answer in a single uninterrupted speech.

title: The Weaver of Family Weather
text: A textile guild's ceremonial tapestry shows each clan's fortunes as stitched constellations, and a junior weaver notices one family has been sewn out of the pattern for generations. Follow her as she investigates without unraveling the cloth.

title: A Verdict in Seven Feathers
text: In a court where birds testify for the dead, a magistrate receives seven feathers from a species believed extinct. Write the judgment she must deliver when each feather seems to accuse a different living person.

title: The Golem's Gardening Leave
text: A clay laborer is granted one week away from the quarry and chooses to cultivate a rooftop garden over the foreman's office. Tell the story of what grows there, and who is changed by tending it.

title: A Recipe for Eating the Moon's Crust
text: A mountain monastery serves a dish said to contain flakes of lunar stone, but its cook learns the ingredient is being mined from a sleeping creature beneath the kitchen. Write the recipe as it is amended during a moral emergency.

title: The Unlicensed Cartographer's Trial
text: A mapmaker is accused of drawing a road that did not exist until people began using it. Prepare a defense speech arguing whether a map can be responsible for the places it brings into being.

title: The Lanterns Beneath the Glacier
text: A team of ice cutters finds a line of lanterns burning beneath clear blue ice, each illuminating a different room in a buried inn. One light goes out whenever someone tells a lie; write the expedition's first night.

title: The Inn at the World's Elbow
text: A roadside inn stands where the continent bends sharply enough to hide one horizon from the other. Invent its regulars and the practical trouble caused by travelers arriving from both sides with incompatible calendars.

title: The Magician Who Hated Applause
text: A stage magician's spells work only while the audience is distracted, so she hires a heckler to keep every eye away from the disappearing act. Write the night the heckler refuses to play along.

title: A Census of the Invisible Herd
text: A royal census taker must count an invisible herd of antelope before the kingdom can tax its migration route. Write a letter to the tax minister as the tally begins to contradict itself, and decide whether the official reports the impossible numbers.

title: The Prince Who Was Allergic to Prophecy
text: Every prediction about the prince causes a different harmless but inconvenient rash, and the court's seers have begun competing to diagnose him. Write a comic scene in which a street fortune-teller offers a cure no one wants to hear.

title: A Mile of Unclaimed Boots
text: After a battlefield is cleared, a cobbler finds a trail of boots walking by themselves toward a village that denies ever sending soldiers. Follow one boot and the person who decides to follow it.

title: The Glassmaker's Second Sky
text: A glassmaker can trap a complete sky inside each pane, but a buyer demands a window showing a day that has not happened yet. Write the negotiation as a tense two-person scene, using only what each can see in the glass.

title: The Parliament of Kitchen Utensils
text: At a royal banquet, the cutlery convenes to decide whether to serve a guest who has never once said thank you. Let the spoon, knife, and serving fork argue from their different duties, then reveal what the guest has come to ask.

title: The Salt Road's New Toll
text: A desert caravan reaches a checkpoint manned by a child collecting one true story from every traveler instead of coins. Write the encounter from the perspective of someone who has survived by telling none.

title: The Clockwork Midwife
text: A brass midwife has delivered generations of children in a mountain town, but now insists that the next birth requires a human apprentice to make a choice no gear can make. Explore their uneasy partnership during one long night.

title: A Field Guide to Borrowed Knees
text: Among the hill folk, people may rent a giant's knees for one day to cross difficult terrain, but the rental office has misplaced a pair. Write a field guide entry that turns into the report of a very inconvenient search.

title: The Last Orchard on the Sun's Back
text: A handful of farmers tend fruit trees on the sun's slow-moving back, harvesting only during eclipses. Their youngest grower discovers a sapling has rooted in a place the sun is trying to keep warm.

title: The Bellows Beneath the City
text: A city breathes through a network of enormous bellows maintained by a disgraced engineer. When the inhalations begin arriving out of rhythm, she must convince the citizens that their streets are alive before they suffocate it.

title: The Duke's Unwanted Familiar
text: A duke's new familiar is a small, solemn creature that eats only signed treaties and has developed a taste for the latest peace accord. Write a short story about the page assigned to keep it fed and the diplomats assigned to stop it.

title: A Letter from the Fifth Chimney
text: A child receives a letter soot-stamped from a chimney that was bricked up before the house was built. Reply to it, deciding what the child is willing to invite into the home.

title: The Surveyor of Sleeping Giants
text: A survey team must redraw the border because a sleeping giant has shifted several miles in its sleep. Write the argument between the two neighboring villages about whether waking it counts as trespass or rescue.

title: The Last Pageant of the Pebble Kings
text: A river valley's pebble-sized monarchs hold a pageant to choose which boulder will become their new palace, while a flood approaches unnoticed by the judges. Tell the story in miniature, keeping the danger grand and the rulers tiny.

title: A School for Unlucky Swords
text: At a boarding school for enchanted blades, one sword refuses to cut anything and keeps interrupting fencing lessons to ask about its maker. Write the first day from the viewpoint of the student assigned to carry it.

title: Three Winters in One Harbor
text: Three nations have agreed to share the season of winter, but a harbor town receives all three winters at once. Write the mayor's letter to the diplomats who will arrive after the thaw, deciding what the town will ask them to change.

title: The Salamander's Union Card
text: Fire salamanders working the royal kilns organize for shorter shifts, and the palace's human furnace-master is told to break the strike before the coronation. Write the negotiations as a screenplay scene with heat rising on every side.

title: A Very Brief History of the Seventh Stair
text: Every staircase in the empire contains one step that leads to a place its builder has never visited. Tell the history of a single such step through the people who find it, in no more than five paragraphs.

title: The Baker's Guild of Fireflies
text: In a city without streetlamps, fireflies are trained to illuminate ovens, but one colony has begun abandoning the bakers to gather around a blind musician. Follow the guild apprentice sent to retrieve them.

title: The Census of Borrowed Faces
text: In a port where masks are inherited like property, a census officer discovers a face registered to a person who has never been born. Write the officer's private report before the family arrives to claim it.

title: The Emperor's Left-Handed Dragon
text: The imperial dragon can only breathe flame to its left, a limitation generations of generals have hidden by rotating the battlefield maps. Write the moment a young tactician must decide whether to preserve the deception or use it.

title: The Village That Measures Its Bread
text: A baker's loaves rise according to the honesty of the neighbors who knead them, leaving the town's most prosperous family with flat bread. Create a warm but unsentimental story about how the village responds to a public breakfast disaster.

title: The Unquiet Brass Compass
text: A compass points toward whichever person in a room most needs to leave, and its owner is hired to settle a family inheritance dispute. Write the meeting as a monologue by the compass, which has its own reasons for wanting everyone out.

title: The Shepherd of Small Volcanoes
text: A shepherd tends a flock of tiny volcanoes whose eruptions fertilize the valley, but one has begun coughing up old coins stamped with the name of a vanished ruler. Tell how the shepherd chooses between pasture and excavation.

title: A Map of the King's Appetite
text: The royal physician charts the king's appetite as shifting terrain, and discovers a new province appearing whenever the monarch refuses a meal. Invent the country's geography and the political crisis its cartographers face.

title: The Apprentice Who Could Taste Numbers
text: A young bookkeeper tastes every number as a different spice, a gift that makes her invaluable to a spice caravan and dangerous to its silent auditor. Write the moment she realizes the missing cargo has a flavor.

title: The Night the Statues Went to Work
text: The city's stone statues have quietly been taking night shifts in the jobs their sculptors once held. One evening, the mason who carved the harbor pilot finds his statue has brought a passenger ashore.

title: A Glossary of Untranslatable Spells
text: An interpreter is assigned to translate a spell whose meaning changes with the listener's childhood dialect. Build a glossary of its failed translations, then let the entries reveal what the interpreter has been avoiding.

title: The Mooncalf at the Tax Office
text: A mooncalf wanders into the municipal tax office and refuses to leave until its grazing rights are recognized. Write a comic story about the junior assessor who must find a category for a creature that weighs less at night.

title: The Queen's Garden of Edible Armor
text: A royal gardener grows protective armor from vegetables, and the palace guard has started eating its supplies before each inspection. Write a letter from the gardener to the queen proposing a solution that could change the kingdom's defenses.

title: The Cartographer's Invisible Ink
text: An ink-maker's maps show a different route to each reader, depending on what they are afraid to find. When a rescue party gets lost despite following the same chart, its maker must decide which fear to address first.

title: The Siege of a Teacup
text: A miniature army has occupied a teacup in a giant's kitchen, defending its last dry ground against the rising wash water. Write their commander’s address to the troops, making clear what victory would cost them.

title: The Choirboy Who Summoned a Jury
text: A novice's hymn accidentally summons twelve ravens, each convinced it has been called to judge the monastery's abbot. Let the boy conduct the hearing and discover what question the birds are actually trying to answer.

title: Letters from the Giant's Cuffs
text: A climber exploring a sleeping giant's coat finds villages stitched into the cuffs, each with its own account of why the giant never wakes. Write letters from the expedition as it nears the giant's wrist, and reveal what the villages fear the climbers will disturb.

title: The Locksmith for Wedding Vows
text: A locksmith crafts tiny mechanisms that keep promises from being broken, and is hired to open one on the eve of a royal marriage. Write a story about what the lock reveals and who truly wants it opened.

title: The Dragon's Annual Dental Inspection
text: A traveling dentist visits a dragon whose teeth have been used as treaty markers for centuries. Write an absurd yet tender scene in which the dragon must decide whether to keep a tooth that bears a nation's border.

title: The Orchard's Unripe Judge
text: In a village court, disputes are settled by a pear grown on the courthouse tree, but this year's fruit will not ripen until both sides agree on what question to ask it. Tell of the case that finally changes the custom.

title: The Tailor of Royal Knees
text: A tailor is commissioned to sew kneepads for a monarch who has never knelt, then receives a second order from the person who expects to make the monarch kneel. Write the tailor's decision in a story focused on craft and complicity.

title: A Kingdom Built on a Sleeping Calf
text: The kingdom's central citadel stands on the back of an enormous calf that has not stirred in five hundred years. When its first twitch cracks the throne room, a stablehand must persuade the court to move before dawn.

title: The Apprentice of Applause
text: In a theater where applause powers the scenery, an apprentice stagehand is ordered to keep clapping after the audience has gone home. Write what the empty seats and the unpowered set show her about the production.

title: The Saffron Trial
text: A spice grows only where someone has changed their mind for a reason they cannot explain, and two rival botanists must prove competing claims to the same field. Present their evidence as a series of field observations with a human cost.

title: The Clockmaker's Crooked Noon
text: A clockmaker builds a timepiece that gives every citizen a different noon, and the city has learned to schedule around the disagreement. When the clock stops, write the first afternoon in which everyone arrives together.

title: The Unruly Atlas of Ants
text: An empire's surveying ants have formed a moving map of a country the emperor insists does not exist. Write from the perspective of the ant keeper asked to erase the map without harming its makers.

title: The Scribe Who Recorded Laughter
text: A court scribe is tasked with documenting every laugh at the royal wedding, though laughter is forbidden in the palace and each recorded one seems to alter the guest list. Tell the story in marginal notes and official entries.

title: A Home for Retired Familiars
text: A sanctuary takes in familiars whose witches have died, left magic, or simply moved on. The newest arrival insists it is still on a mission and persuades a wary caretaker to help complete it.

title: The Ferryman's Weight Limit
text: A ferryman can carry only what a passenger is willing to name, and a silent traveler arrives with a cart full of heavy, unmarked crates. Write their crossing as a negotiation in which every refusal changes the boat.

title: The Prince of Borrowed Elbows
text: A prince born without elbows can bend his arms only by asking another person to lend theirs for a moment. On the day he must sign a peace accord, his usual lender is on the opposing delegation; write the encounter.

title: The Great Glass Migration
text: Once a century, every glass object in a valley walks toward the mountains, leaving households to choose what they can safely keep. Write a family story about the one pane of glass that refuses the journey.

title: An Etiquette for Meeting Your Future Statue
text: A sculptor's unfinished figures occasionally step down from their plinths to ask why they were made. Compose a formal etiquette guide for patrons, then let one encounter break every rule in it.

title: The City Beneath the Violin
text: A violinist discovers a city of tiny residents living inside her instrument, where every note changes their buildings and every pause is a public emergency. Tell the story of the concert she cannot cancel.

title: The Salt-Lick for Unicorns
text: A herder maintains a mineral spring for unicorns that have forgotten how to recognize purity, and a traveling judge asks to drink from it before sentencing a thief. Explore what the herder chooses to disclose.

title: The Siege Accountant’s Arithmetic
text: During a siege, an accountant finds that every bucket of water recorded as lost appears in a different household's well. Write letters from the accountant to the besieging and defending leaders before the next rationing bell forces both sides to act.

title: The Queen's Borrowed Stomach
text: A monarch's hunger has been transferred into a palace cook to spare the kingdom from famine omens, but the cook has begun craving the crown's forbidden iron fruit. Write a monologue delivered in the kitchens after midnight.

title: A Cartload of Unclaimed Thunder
text: A traveling smith sells thunder by the pound to villages that need storms for their mills, but one barrel has started answering questions. Write the exchange between smith and buyer as they decide whether to open it.

title: The Parliament of Unfinished Statues
text: Sculptors leave abandoned figures in a quarry where they gather to debate which of them deserves completion. A new apprentice arrives to select stone for the city's founder; invent the quarrel that changes her commission.

title: The Day the Mountains Went on Strike
text: The mountain range refuses to hold up the sky until the valley towns stop blasting tunnels through its feet. Write a screenplay scene between a union negotiator, a mining foreman, and the child who can translate stone.

title: A Field Note on Domestic Wyverns
text: A naturalist studying tiny house-wyverns finds that each family has trained its animal to guard a different kind of secret. Write a field note about the one household whose wyvern guards something no one admits is missing.

title: The Queen's Tournament of Ordinary Skills
text: The queen hosts a contest in which champions compete at mending socks, peeling onions, and carrying sleeping children without waking them. Create a story about the unexpected finalist and the court's shifting idea of strength.

title: The Moon's Unpaid Ferryman
text: A ferryman transports moonbeams from one side of the world to the other, but has not been paid since the moon changed its orbit. Write his petitioning letter to the celestial labor court, including the evidence he brings.

title: The Unraveling of Captain Bracken's Coat
text: A sea captain's coat is woven from the names of every port she has visited; after a mutiny, the names begin slipping loose and appearing on the wrong shore. Tell the story of her return to the first place she erased.

title: The Glass-Eyed Orchardist
text: An orchardist replaces one eye with a glass lens that sees how each fruit will be eaten, and begins avoiding trees whose harvests end badly. Write the day a hungry stranger asks her to choose a peach.

title: A Constitution for the Crawling Palace
text: The royal palace moves on hundreds of wooden legs and has developed opinions about where the court should live. Draft a short constitution governing its right to refuse relocation, then show the first dispute under that law.

title: The Baker Who Could Not Lie About Flour
text: A baker's flour reveals any lie told while kneading it, and the magistrate orders her to supply bread for a diplomatic banquet. Write the story of the secret that comes to light before dessert.

title: The Wasp Duke's Summer Court
text: A wasp duke holds court inside a hollow apple and demands a human advocate after the orcharders petition to burn the tree. Write the advocate's opening statement, balancing the orchard's livelihood against the colony's claim.

title: The Apprentice Who Mended Borders
text: A royal seamstress repairs torn borders on the kingdom's ceremonial maps with thread that also joins the actual lands together. When a neighboring country requests a patch, she must decide what the seam should include.

title: The Dovecote of Unsent Decrees
text: A palace dovecote houses messages the rulers decided not to send, each pigeon carrying the consequences of a different silence. A new keeper finds one bird that has escaped and returned with a reply.

title: The Last Witness to the First Sunrise
text: In a world where dawn began only after a council voted to permit it, one ancient witness remembers the first morning and opposes a proposal to shorten the day. Write her testimony before a generation that has never seen a full sunrise.

title: A Pocket Guide to Courting a Basilisk
text: A junior royal envoy must negotiate with a basilisk whose courtship customs involve exchanging carefully selected stones without looking directly at one another. Write the envoy's field guide, including the mistake that nearly turns diplomacy to sculpture.

title: The Innkeeper's Unlicensed Constellation
text: An innkeeper has painted a private constellation on the ceiling to help homesick guests navigate their dreams, but the stars have begun rearranging themselves around a newly arrived traveler. Tell what the innkeeper learns by staying awake.

title: The Trial of the Borrowed Tongue
text: A translator is accused of giving a dragon's speech the wrong meaning, though the dragon itself insists it never spoke. Write the courtroom exchange in which gesture, silence, and punctuation matter more than vocabulary.

title: The Cobbler's Seven-League Misfit
text: A cobbler accidentally makes one shoe that carries its wearer seven leagues and the other that keeps them exactly where they stand. Write a comic story about a courier who must deliver a fragile wedding cake across the kingdom.

title: A Parliament for the Last Wildflower
text: A town council convenes to decide whether to pave over the only wildflower left in a valley, unaware that the flower has sent a delegate. Let its advocate argue for a future the council cannot yet imagine.

title: The Alchemist's Unfinished Shadow Puppet
text: An alchemist invents a puppet that can reenact any choice its owner regrets, but the puppet begins performing a decision the alchemist has not made yet. Write the story as a sequence of short scenes separated by stage directions.

title: The Harvest of Brass Birds
text: Each autumn, brass birds descend on the rooftops to collect the town's unused words, leaving people fluent in everything except what they meant to say. Follow a sign painter who invents a new alphabet before the next flock arrives.

title: The Cartographer of Magnetic Tides
text: A surveyor on a moon with a shifting iron core must chart safe routes for a migration fleet before the landscape's compasses become useless. Her maps are the only record of a path her own family refuses to take.

title: Three Harvests on Europa
text: A hydroponics apprentice discovers that one algae crop has started converting waste into a compound that slows aging, but the station's ration board plans to destroy it as a contamination risk. Write the dispute through the apprentice's work log and the board's inspection notes.

title: The Orbital Debris Choir
text: A salvage pilot learns to read the changing harmonics of tumbling satellites and realizes a debris field is about to strike a school shuttle. Give the pilot one hour, a failing tug, and a reason not to reveal how they know.

title: A Treaty in Salt
text: On a dry planet where water rights are inherited through mineral claims, a mediator must settle a boundary dispute after two rival wells break into the same underground brine sea. Make the geology complicate what the law calls ownership.

title: The Child Who Outgrew Her Gravity
text: A child raised in low gravity returns to Earth for a custody hearing and finds every ordinary gesture newly exhausting. Let the adults argue over her future while she quietly tests what her body can still do.

title: Night Soil for a Ringworld
text: A sanitation crew on a habitat ring discovers that the station's nutrient loop has been diverting human waste into a sealed district whose residents were told their crops were synthetic. Write a tense shift in which a practical repair becomes a question of consent.

title: The Longest Elevator Ride
text: A lift carries ore between the surface and a mine beneath a planet's deep ice, taking six hours each way. On one descent, the cargo begins to warm despite the crew's records showing no power source aboard.

title: Sparrow Protocol
text: A planetary ecologist is assigned to remove an imported bird from a sealed colony, only to find that the bird's nesting habits have become the habitat's most reliable pollination system. Let the removal order arrive on the eve of the colony's first harvest.

title: The Unmapped Side of the Sun
text: A solar-sail navigator accepts a delivery route that keeps the ship permanently outside direct radio contact. Halfway through, the vessel's shadow begins to fall at an angle the star charts cannot explain.

title: A Bench for the Unborn
text: In a city where embryo selection is publicly funded, a furniture maker is hired to build a memorial bench for genetic traits that were never chosen. Their commission becomes personal when a customer asks for a place to grieve a child who was never conceived.

title: The Last Shift at Ceres Foundry
text: A foundry's workers are told their jobs will be automated after one final production run, but the machine's safety model has omitted the faint tremor that only veteran operators can feel. Write from the perspective of the youngest worker, who must decide whether to trust the data or the crew.

title: The Last Counterweight at Vesta
text: A mass driver on Vesta uses a captured nickel boulder as its counterweight, and the boulder also anchors the mining town's water tanks. A change in launch trajectory forces the engineer to choose between releasing the load for a critical shipment and keeping the town's water system intact.

title: The Lunar Seed Auction
text: Families bid for the right to grow the first open-air crop beneath a lunar dome, where each seed variety can survive only one season. A quiet bidder enters with no money, but a sample of soil collected before the dome was built.

title: A Very Small Black Hole
text: A university lab's tabletop gravity experiment creates a stable distortion just large enough to bend dust into a miniature orbit. The night custodian notices the orbit has acquired a second, irregular particle that moves like it is avoiding something.

title: The Plastic Reef
text: A community living on floating salvage platforms has cultivated a reef from engineered polymer that filters toxins but slowly consumes the structures holding the town together. Ask a boatwright to choose which part of home to sacrifice first.

title: The Captain's Unpaid Cargo
text: A freighter captain accepts an unregistered shipment of soil from a planet whose export laws forbid removing anything alive. At the destination, the cargo begins producing spores that thrive in the ship's air filters.

title: Five Minutes of Local Sun
text: A mountain settlement on a tidally locked world receives sunlight through a moving mirror for five minutes each month. The mirror operator is asked to redirect the beam toward a hospital instead of the communal greenhouse.

title: When the Ice Remembers Pressure
text: A glaciologist on an inhabited comet drills into ice compressed by centuries of passing ships and uncovers a layer shaped by a vessel that has not yet arrived. Keep the mystery grounded in competing physical explanations.

title: The Spare Lung Clinic
text: A transplant clinic grows replacement lungs from patients' own cells, but a batch arrives with a harmless variation that makes recipients breathe more efficiently at high altitude. A mountain rescue worker asks for one despite not being sick.

title: Salt Maps the Future
text: On a remote asteroid, a geologist finds a salt vein that forms tiny building models whenever exposed to station light. One crystal matches a habitat design no one has made yet, down to a hidden storage room the crew has not discovered.

title: The Quiet Market on Ganymede
text: At an unlicensed market beneath Ganymede's ice, a cook trades recipes made from foods that cannot legally be grown in the corporate habitat. An inspector arrives hungry, carrying an order to shut the stalls before a visiting delegation sees them.

title: Antenna for the Blind Spot
text: An engineer builds a radio antenna inside a crater shielded from every known transmission, hoping to give a remote settlement privacy. The first thing it receives is a precise map of the antenna's own construction, including a bolt the engineer forgot to install.

title: The Year of the Extra Monsoon
text: Climate engineers can redirect one storm system to save a coastal city, but doing so will end the only wet season of a neighboring agrarian moon colony. Tell the story through the weather forecaster's final public briefing and the messages they choose not to read aloud.

title: A Window on the Exoplanet
text: A technician replacing the glass in a generation ship's observation bay discovers a hairline crack that reveals the star field moving differently from the navigation display. The repair manual says to seal it; the ship's oldest passenger asks for one more night to look.

title: Proof of Soil
text: A court on a newly settled planet must decide whether imported Earth soil counts as property, biological heritage, or evidence of an ecological crime. Draft the testimony of a farmer whose field contains all three.

title: The Antenna Shepherd
text: A keeper on a plateau walks each evening among enormous steerable antenna dishes, guiding them away from lightning without interrupting their research. One dish begins tracking a storm that will never reach the ground.

title: The Oxygen Dividend
text: A corporation offers residents a monthly payment for breathing less during peak demand, using wearable monitors to calculate their share of the habitat's recycled air. A marathon runner accepts the contract, then discovers the system is charging a sick neighbor for every deep breath.

title: The Unfinished Language of Hands
text: A crew of deaf engineers on a noisy mining moon invents a compact signing system for work beyond radio range. When a new contractor arrives, the crew must choose between teaching the signs that keep them safe and protecting the private grammar they built together.

title: An Orchard in Transit
text: A transport ship carries grafted fruit trees to a new settlement, but the roots have grown through the crates and into the ship's coolant lines. The botanist wants to save the orchard; the pilot calculates that saving it will cost their return fuel.

title: The Museum of Unlicensed Machines
text: In a cramped border station, a mechanic preserves obsolete devices that were outlawed because they cannot be remotely disabled. A child brings in a broken toy and asks whether its maker can still be held responsible for what it learns.

title: One Planet, Two Noon Bells
text: A valley's two settlements use different orbital calendars, so their noon bells drift apart by several minutes each season. When an emergency siren sounds between them, a schoolteacher must decide which signal the children have been taught to trust.

title: The Crater That Keeps Its Heat
text: A geothermal survey team finds a small crater that remains warm through the planet's long winter, though every instrument says its rock should be cold. Give the youngest technician a scientific explanation they desperately hope is true and a personal reason to doubt it.

title: Renting the View
text: A high-rise habitat sells residents timed access to its only window facing the blue planet below. A window attendant starts letting one elderly tenant stay after closing, unaware that the tenant has been leaving something for the people in the queue.

title: The Manual Override
text: During a colony's annual blackout drill, a new safety officer discovers that the emergency doors have been designed to open only from the outside. Their supervisor insists the configuration is intentional; the drill begins in four minutes.

title: A Planet Made of Pumice
text: A geologist landing on a porous volcanic world finds that footsteps leave no prints but do change how sound travels beneath the surface. Compose the expedition's first field report as its author gradually realizes the team's equipment is making the terrain unstable.

title: The Kelp Line's Winter
text: On an ocean planet, a diver cultivates kelp along a thermal boundary that rises and falls with the twin suns. When the boundary begins dropping faster than forecasts, she must choose which beds to abandon while her sister's research station insists the readings are instrument drift.

title: A Kitchen at the Edge of Mars
text: The cook at a remote rover depot prepares a meal for a crew that has just learned their return window is delayed by two years. Each person requests a dish from a different place they may never visit again.

title: The Little Engine in the Floodplain
text: A century-old flood barrier is operated by an autonomous engine too small to appear on modern infrastructure maps. When a settlement upstream expands, the machine begins diverting water toward an abandoned riverbed instead of the new reservoir.

title: The Trial of the First Fossil
text: A paleontologist finds a fossil on a world where life was engineered from Earth organisms, and the discovery threatens to overturn the settlement's founding charter. Write the hearing as a contest between the scientist, the charter's author, and a child who has named the specimen.

title: A Constellation of Work Lights
text: On a construction platform beyond Neptune, crews arrange their work lamps into patterns visible from the next shift's docking path. A new worker changes one light to signal danger, but the old hands mistake it for a greeting.

title: The Pollen Passport
text: A botanist's travel permit is rejected because the grains on her coat match a plant declared extinct on her homeworld. She has never seen the species, yet its pollen keeps appearing wherever she has slept.

title: The Reservoir Beneath the Stadium
text: A city converts its old stadium into a reservoir after years of drought, and divers find a sealed maintenance tunnel under the lowest seats. Inside are hand-painted depth marks that count down from a water level the city has never reached.

title: A Brief History of the Failed Dome
text: A settlement historian must write the official account of a transparent habitat that shattered during its first winter, but every survivor remembers a different sound before the collapse. Frame the history as three incompatible drafts and leave the reader to infer what was omitted.

title: The Lunar Customs Declaration
text: A customs officer on a moon base must inspect a returning crew member's permitted cargo: one living insect, one cup of regolith, and one object not made by humans. The crew member's answers are technically correct and increasingly alarming.

title: An Engineered Accent
text: A settlement's children grow up hearing the same standardized announcements through ceiling speakers, yet each neighborhood develops a distinct rhythm of speech. A linguist sent to document the change discovers that the accents are forming around local machine faults.

title: The Weight of a Tiny Planet
text: A survey team working inside a hollowed asteroid discovers that its artificial gravity shifts whenever one crew member leaves the habitat. Their calculations suggest the asteroid is responding not to mass but to a pattern of movement.

title: The Reef's New Tenants
text: A marine architect must redesign an underwater city after an engineered coral species colonizes the supports and begins sheltering wild fish that residents have never encountered. The council wants a clean removal; the maintenance divers have other plans.

title: A Suit with No Owner
text: After a routine EVA, a station's inventory registers an extra spacesuit, still warm and carrying a fresh pressure seal. The crew's safety officer has one hour to find its owner before the next airlock cycle.

title: How to Grow a Mountain
text: A terraforming cooperative can raise a mountain range by heating buried mineral seams, but the new highlands will alter wind and water across three settlements. Write a field guide for residents who must decide whether the proposed skyline is worth its cost.

title: The Silence Between Launches
text: At a commercial spaceport, an acoustic engineer is hired to reduce noise pollution for nearby residents. She discovers that one launch's low-frequency vibration makes a locked storage container open a fraction of an inch each time.

title: The Day the Map Was Too Accurate
text: An underground courier uses a navigation system that updates faster than the city's official plans. When it begins routing her through spaces that have not been built yet, she follows one path to deliver medicine to a patient whose address does not exist.

title: The Last Tree in the Gravity Well
text: A botanist tends a single Earth tree inside a rotating habitat whose spin will soon be reduced to save power. The tree has grown around a structural brace, and moving it would expose the habitat to a risk nobody has calculated.

title: A Message in the Machine's Accent
text: A speech synthesizer used by emergency dispatchers develops a regional accent after years of imitating thousands of callers. One night, it pronounces a street name in a way that leads a dispatcher to question the official location of a fire.

title: Dust Rights at Dawn
text: Farmers on a terraformed plateau are allowed a fixed number of dust-control drones, but a new family of migratory gliders nests in the drone sheds. The local organizer must argue for the creatures before the next forecasted storm.

title: The Shape of a Safe Landing
text: A pilot on a low-gravity world is ordered to land on a perfectly flat pad, but the only available surface is a slope covered in fragile mineral blooms. Make the landing a negotiation among physics, corporate procedure, and the person waiting below.

title: The Apprentice Who Counts Cracks
text: A junior inspector on a generation ship maps hairline fractures in the walls, using their spread to learn the ship's forgotten maintenance history. One crack passes through a sealed cabin door that the manifest lists as empty space.

title: The Company That Sold Its Horizon
text: A mining settlement has leased the rights to its horizon, allowing a distant corporation to project advertisements across the sky. The first projection blocks the residents' view of a navigation beacon, and the contract's cancellation clause is written in a language no one locally speaks.

title: A Seed for the Dark Side
text: A plant breeder is asked to create a crop that can grow without sunlight in a permanently shadowed crater. Her successful prototype produces a scent that draws a native animal out of its underground refuge.

title: The Unscheduled Child
text: A family aboard a long-haul vessel welcomes a baby born outside the ship's approved population plan. The nurse must decide whether to alter the manifest before the arrival port's automated immigration system counts the new passenger as excess mass.

title: The Colony's First Ambulance
text: A settlement has built its first ground vehicle, but no one agrees what emergency it should answer first: an injured miner, a stranded survey team, or a herd of imported animals loose near the airlocks. Follow its inaugural dispatch.

title: The Tide Gauge in the Desert
text: A hydrologist finds an old tide gauge standing in a dry inland basin, its needle rising at the same hour each day. The basin's inhabitants insist the device measures something more important than water.

title: The Repair Shop for Satellites
text: A family-run workshop catches dead satellites in a net and refurbishes them for small communities. A customer brings a unit that still has a valid warranty, though its maker went bankrupt before the family was born.

title: A Light That Costs Nothing
text: A rural settlement receives a device that converts waste heat into a steady lamp, apparently free of charge. The inventor left no instructions, and the lamp grows brighter whenever someone nearby tells the truth about why they moved there.

title: The Seat That Faces Away
text: On a diplomatic shuttle, every passenger seat faces the shared table except one, which points toward the hull. A newly appointed interpreter is assigned that seat and discovers the shuttle's crew has been withholding a view from the delegation.

title: The Waterline on the Wedding Wall
text: A couple on a floating city marks each anniversary by recording the waterline on their kitchen wall, though the city rises and falls with no predictable sea. On the year they plan to leave, the mark appears before the tide does.

title: The Pioneer's Unsent Blueprint
text: An architect hired to recreate a famous early habitat finds a set of unpublished plans that would have made the structure easier to live in but harder to govern. Decide whether the new build should honor the original design or its unbuilt alternative.

title: An Animal for the Airlock
text: A rescue station keeps a small, carefully trained animal to detect carbon dioxide leaks, a task no sensor has matched reliably. When a funding audit orders its retirement, the station's newest technician must prove its value without putting it at risk.

title: Letters from a Failed Terraformer
text: A former engineer returns to a planet where their first climate-control project failed and now lives among communities that adapted to the altered seasons. Write letters to the people who trusted the project, letting field observations give way to personal apologies.

title: The Exoplanet's Crooked River
text: A river on a low-gravity planet flows uphill for several kilometers before spilling into the sea, driven by a wind pattern visible only from a balloon. A local guide takes a visiting hydrologist to the bend where the current changes direction without warning.

title: A Contract for One More Breath
text: A miner trapped in a damaged pressure tunnel can be rescued only if a nearby settlement redirects its last emergency oxygen reserve. The trapped worker once wrote the rule that forbids this exchange; let both sides make their case over a failing comm line.

title: The Planetary Park Ranger
text: A ranger assigned to protect an alien wilderness must explain why a dangerous patch of luminous moss cannot be harvested for medicine, even though the only known cure grows on it. Their first visitor is a child with a parent already sick.

title: The Clockwork of a Tidal Lock
text: A clockmaker on a tidally locked moon builds a public clock that tracks the narrow band of dusk where life can survive outdoors. The clock begins losing time, but only on days when the settlement's elected council meets.

title: A City Built Around a Crater
text: A new transit tunnel through a crater wall uncovers old foundations that predate the colony's official landing. A construction foreman must halt work while officials debate whether the structures are geological, human, or something the settlement's history cannot accommodate.

title: The Collector of Failed Experiments
text: A retired lab assistant keeps discarded prototypes from projects that never passed review, each labeled with the reason it was rejected. A young inventor asks for the one device whose rejection note reads only: 'It worked.'

title: The Aquarium on a Comet
text: A traveling science exhibit carries a sealed tank of microbes through the outer system, relying on comet water to keep the ecosystem stable. A student guide notices that the smallest organisms are rearranging the tank's mineral sediment into a precise spiral.

title: A Map of Future Shade
text: A city planner on a planet with a rapidly shifting axial tilt must design streets that will remain cool for the next fifty years. Her most accurate model makes the historic district uninhabitable, including the house where the planning office began.

title: The Music of a Pressure Hull
text: A ship's hull makes different notes as its temperature changes, and the crew's mechanic has learned to tune the panels by ear. During a quiet crossing, she hears a tone that matches a warning signal from a vessel lost long before her birth.

title: The Neighborhood Under the Landing Pad
text: Workers widening a spaceport discover an entire neighborhood beneath a concrete landing pad, its residents living in a pressure-stable cavity omitted from every construction plan. The first person to climb down is the project manager's estranged sibling.

title: A Species on the Payroll
text: A mining company hires a xenobiologist to prove that a newly found organism is not intelligent and therefore does not qualify for habitat protections. The organism has already adapted its growth cycle to interrupt the mine's loudest machinery.

title: The Final Test of the Skyhook
text: A crew prepares the first test of a cable linking a planet's surface to orbit, but the cable's small vibrations are interfering with a nearby community's navigation instruments. The test director must decide whether postponement is caution or a surrender to bad engineering.

title: A Postcard from the Interior
text: A geologist who has spent decades mapping a hollow asteroid sends the family at its surface entrance a postcard describing a warm wind from a region the latest scans show is solid rock. Write the postcard before deciding whether the geologist will descend again.

title: The Habitat with Two Kitchens
text: A research station has separate kitchens for its human crew and its symbiotic microbial workers, whose needs are translated into temperature and mineral schedules. A food shortage forces the new quartermaster to decide which menu will be simplified first.

title: The Weather inside the Suit
text: An EVA trainee's suit develops a tiny internal climate: a dry breeze on the left side, condensation on the right, and a brief frost whenever the trainee thinks about home. The instructor treats it as a sensor fault until the trainee asks to keep the suit for one more walk.

title: A Bridge for the Slow Ship
text: A remote station must build a docking arm for a generation ship moving too slowly to maneuver, using only materials already on site. The crew's best design depends on a structural component that the station's residents regard as sacred infrastructure.

title: The Planetary Seed Library
text: A librarian on a terraformed world lends seed packets under the same rules as books, including fines for late returns. One borrower returns a packet with a plant that has evolved beyond the catalog's description during a single growing season.

title: The Miner Who Heard the Mantle
text: A deep-crust driller claims the planet's mantle is producing a rhythm that changes when the drill pauses. The geology team dismisses the pattern until the miner asks them to stop before the next shift begins.

title: The White Line Across the Dome
text: A hairline white streak appears across the interior of a settlement dome, moving a few centimeters each day despite stable pressure readings. The painter assigned to cover it recognizes a pattern from an old navigation chart and must convince the maintenance chief before the next dust storm.

title: A Field Guide to Unfamiliar Rain
text: Write a field guide for settlers who have never experienced liquid rain, describing how to distinguish harmless precipitation from the corrosive seasonal downpour. Thread the practical directions with the guide author's account of the first roof they lost.

title: The Evacuation of One Street
text: A small asteroid settlement must move a single street of homes before an automated mining route passes through, but each house is bolted into the same shared life-support loop. Let the street's residents negotiate what can be carried and what must be disconnected.

title: The Colony That Grew Sideways
text: A colony's first generation adapts to a planet whose strongest winds blow parallel to the ground, shaping buildings, crops, and even how children learn to walk. A visiting inspector insists the settlement is unsafe because it violates standards written for upright worlds.

title: The Smallest Moon in the System
text: An astronomer discovers that a pebble-sized moon has been captured by a planet's rings, completing one orbit every few minutes. A child at the observatory asks what could possibly be worth naming something so temporary.

title: The Exchange of Empty Bottles
text: On a long interplanetary route, travelers trade empty drink containers as keepsakes, each bottle marked with the point where it was finished. A courier receives one from a passenger whose itinerary shows they never boarded.

title: A Song for the Pressure Door
text: A station's maintenance crew sings a work cadence to coordinate the slow movement of a massive pressure door. When budget cuts replace the crew with a silent control system, one mechanic keeps singing and discovers the door has begun responding to the rhythm.

title: The Archive of Soil Samples
text: A planetary lab stores soil samples by coordinates, but a new curator finds that several sealed vials have been relabeled with the names of people who lived near the sampling sites. One name belongs to someone still waiting outside the lab.

title: The Last Bus through the Dome
text: A settlement's final public bus route runs through a greenhouse corridor scheduled for conversion into a private research wing. Its driver begins making unscheduled stops so passengers can gather cuttings before the gates close.

title: The Unstable North
text: Compasses on a young planet point toward a magnetic pole that wanders several kilometers each day, disrupting a caravan's navigation. The caravan's guide insists the changing direction is useful, but refuses to say what it reveals.

title: A Theater for One Atmosphere
text: A traveling performance troupe can stage its show only in habitats with a specific pressure and gas mix, limiting its audience to a handful of moons. When a venue offers to simulate the conditions at great expense, the actors must decide whether the performance will still mean the same thing.

title: The Salvage Rights of a Wreck
text: A tug crew reaches a derelict freighter whose registration was erased when its home government dissolved. Three neighboring settlements claim the wreck, but the tug pilot finds evidence that its cargo was meant for none of them.

title: A Second Horizon
text: After an atmospheric experiment, residents of a desert planet see a thin blue band above the horizon each evening, though the planet has no moon and no nearby ocean. A photographer's negatives show the band widening in the direction of an abandoned test range.

title: The Settlement's Borrowed River
text: A colony diverts a seasonal meltwater channel through its first city, promising to restore the riverbed once the settlement is self-sufficient. Years later, the river's original valley has become a living community that cannot survive the promised restoration.

title: Salt Ledger at Low Tide
text: A coastal archivist finds that the names in a nineteenth-century ship ledger wash off only during unusually low tides. The newest blank line matches the handwriting of a living deckhand who has never been near the sea.

title: The Orchard's Unripe Teeth
text: A migrant fruit picker discovers hard white objects inside every peach on one neglected row; the foreman insists they are stones and orders the crop shipped before sunrise. Decide what the picker risks by opening one in front of the crew.

title: Emergency Contact: None
text: During a night shift at a rural clinic, a receptionist must complete the emergency-contact fields for a patient who has no pulse but keeps correcting the spelling of relatives' names. Write the scene through the receptionist's careful, increasingly compromised professionalism.

title: A Choir for the Condemned Mine
text: A mining town's memorial choir is asked to perform underground, where the last rescue team disappeared. The conductor recognizes a harmony that only her brother used to sing, though he never worked in the mine.

title: The Seamstress Counts to Nine
text: A costume repairer mends a burial shroud whose seams keep splitting into nine equal sections. When the deceased's family arrives early, the repairer must choose whether to hand over the unfinished garment or explain what is being stitched into it.

title: Beneath the Municipal Pool
text: A maintenance apprentice finds a dry, tiled corridor under the public pool, though the building has no basement on its plans. At closing time, wet footprints begin climbing the corridor's walls toward the apprentice's tools.

title: The Candle Auction
text: At an estate auction, bidders compete for a box of half-burned candles labeled with dates that have not happened yet. The auctioneer recognizes one date as the night she promised to stay with her ill father.

title: A Patient Map of Bruises
text: A prison doctor charts bruises that appear on inmates before they are injured, each mark tracing a route through the prison's sealed wing. Let the doctor decide whether to follow the map or protect a patient who knows where it leads.

title: The Bellmaker's Deaf Apprentice
text: A deaf apprentice can feel a new bell's vibrations spelling a name no one has taught them. The bellmaker plans to install it above the town's evacuation siren, and the apprentice must make themselves understood before the first test.

title: Supper at the Flood Line
text: After a levee breaks, a stranded family shares a meal on the upper floor of a roadside diner while something below keeps tapping the submerged windows in time with their forks. Give each diner a different reason to pretend the sound is ordinary.

title: The Tenant of Room 0B
text: A housing inspector finds an apartment numbered 0B between the ground floor and the basement, occupied by a tenant whose lease is older than the building. The inspector has one afternoon to certify the property before the demolition crew arrives.

title: The Conservator's Night Letter
text: A museum conservator receives a sealed specimen jar containing a hand whose fingerprints change each night. Write to the museum director in a series of letters, trying to remain professional as each report becomes a plea for help.

title: The Ambulance That Takes the Long Way
text: An ambulance crew is sent to a routine call on a familiar road, but every detour brings them past the same abandoned roadside shrine with a fresh offering. The patient insists they must not reach the hospital before the next hour.

title: Black Thread in the Snowpack
text: A backcountry ranger finds black thread running beneath the snow, taut between trees and warm to the touch. A lost skier has tied their mittens to it, and the ranger must decide whether to follow the line uphill or cut it.

title: The Children's Museum After Dark
text: An overnight guard notices that the museum's life-size dioramas have been rearranged to show the guard's childhood home, down to a broken kitchen tile. In the morning, a school group is due to enter the exhibit.

title: A Recipe for Uninvited Guests
text: A village baker inherits a recipe that requires one extra portion for a guest no one may describe. On the first night she skips the portion, her regular customers begin arriving with unfamiliar apologies.

title: The Floodplain Survey
text: Two surveyors mark a new floodplain and find a line of small doors set into the mud, each opening onto a dry room containing one of their personal belongings. The junior surveyor wants to report the discovery; the senior has already selected a door.

title: Practice Room 6
text: A conservatory student rehearses alone in a soundproof room where the metronome steadily accelerates despite being unplugged. The student must finish a public audition piece while deciding which notes are coming from the instrument and which from the walls.

title: The Town's Borrowed Ambulance
text: A remote town borrows an ambulance from a neighboring district, but every patient transported in it arrives with a second, impossible diagnosis written on the windshield. The driver tries to return the vehicle before the next call comes in.

title: A Census of Empty Nests
